A.explanation: One arrow is reversed so the three vectors do not follow head-to-tail in the same sense and cannot give zero resultant for constant speed.

B.explanation: One arrow is reversed so the vector triangle does not close in the same rotational direction and cannot represent balanced weight, normal contact force and friction.

C.explanation: One arrow is reversed so the head-to-tail chain does not make a continuous loop and cannot give the zero net force required.

D.explanation: All three arrows follow head-to-tail in the same sense to form a closed triangle, giving zero resultant as required for rolling at constant speed.

hints: Notice the ball rolls down the slope at constant speed, so the resultant of weight, normal force and friction must be zero.
Recall the fixed directions: weight acts vertically down, the normal contact force acts perpendicular away from the slope, and friction acts parallel up the slope.
Place the three vectors head-to-tail: for zero resultant they must join to make a closed triangle with all arrows running the same way round - check which diagram keeps that circulation.
walkthrough: Constant speed in a straight direction means acceleration is zero, so by Newton's first law the vector sum of the three forces must be zero.

Identify the three directions: weight $W$ is vertically downward, normal force $N$ is perpendicular to the slope surface, friction $F$ is parallel to the slope and up the slope opposing the downward rolling.
For three non-parallel forces to sum to zero, when drawn head-to-tail they must form a closed triangle.
That closure requires a continuous circulation: the head of one vector is the tail of the next, with all arrows pointing the same way round the triangle.
Three of the diagrams break this circulation because one side has its arrow pointing opposite to the loop, which would leave a non-zero resultant.
Only one diagram has the vertical-down weight, the up-slope friction and the slope-normal force joining head-to-tail in one consistent sense to close the triangle. This is option D.
